task: 0.2 — Add installation and resolution acceptance checks
revisionNote: Revises revision 3 after a third review pass found one more hole: revision 3's own new root-lock-agreement check silently passed (ok:true) when the lock's root record (`packages['']`) was absent entirely, because it treated 'no record' as 'nothing to compare' instead of a failure, on the mistaken assumption that some other check already covered that case. Reproduced with a standalone repro script before fixing, per this repo's working standard. See revision4FollowUp. Revisions 2-3 sections below are otherwise unchanged as a historical record.

revision4FollowUp.claim: lock.cjs silently returns success when lock.packages[''] is missing, claiming another check reports it. No other check does.
revision4FollowUp.reproducedBeforeFixing: Built a full synthetic lock (18 workspace records + node_modules links, both excluded-project locks present) with the `packages['']` root record entirely absent, and called `lock.run({rootDir})` directly: returned `{ok: true, failures: []}`.
revision4FollowUp.rootCause: `checkRootDependencyDeclarationsMatchManifest` (added in revision 2) did `if (!record) return failures;` -- an empty array, not a failure -- on the assumption stated in its own comment that a missing root record was 'a structural problem reported elsewhere'. No other function in lock.cjs (checkLockfileVersion, checkWorkspaceRecordsAndLinks, checkNoBackendChildLocks, checkExcludedLocksPreserved) ever inspects `packages['']` at all, so that assumption was false and the root dependency-agreement check could be bypassed outright by deleting one lock entry.
revision4FollowUp.fix: A missing root record now pushes an explicit failure ('Root lock has no record for the root package itself; root dependency agreement cannot be verified.') instead of returning early with no failures.

run() fails end-to-end when the root lock has no record for the root package
revision4FollowUp.reviewersExactReproReRun: Re-ran the reviewer's exact scenario (18 workspace records/links + both excluded locks, root record omitted) after the fix: `{ok: false, failures: 1}`, the failure naming the missing packages[''] record.

reviewFindingsAddressed.claim: Workspace engines are still unchecked: a fixture with all 18 expected workspaces declaring `engines.node: <20` made both `manifests` and `engines` return ok:true.
reviewFindingsAddressed.reproducedBeforeFixing: Built a synthetic 18-workspace fixture (all EXPECTED_WORKSPACES, correct @bitpay-labs/<dir> names, COMPILE_ORDER packages given a `compile` script to isolate the engines question from unrelated compile-membership noise) with every manifest declaring `engines.node: "<20"`. `manifests.run({structureOnly:true})` returned ok:true, and a synthetic root lock with `link:true` entries for each workspace made `engines.run()` also return ok:true, 0 failures.
reviewFindingsAddressed.rootCause: engines.cjs's `collectInstalledEngineDeclarations` explicitly did `if (record.link) continue;` for every workspace-link lock entry, and separately skipped any key not containing 'node_modules/' -- so a workspace's own top-level lock record (e.g. `packages['packages/bitcore-lib']`) was never reachable either. No mode anywhere evaluated a workspace's own declared `engines.node`. My earlier revision-2 defense of this skip (reasoning that 'root policy in manifests already governs it') was wrong: `manifests`'s root-identity check only validates the *root* package.json's own `engines.node`, never any individual workspace's.
reviewFindingsAddressed.fix: engines.cjs now resolves each `record.link` entry to its real workspace directory (`record.resolved`) and evaluates that workspace's own installed manifest exactly like any other dependency, per acceptance-spec §3's literal text ('Resolve workspace links to their real packages'), which I had previously misread as already satisfied.

semverDependency.problem: package.json declared `semver: ^7.6.3` as a direct devDependency, but package-lock.json was never regenerated for it. `npm ls semver` reported the root project's own dependency as invalid: root resolved to the pre-existing hoisted semver@5.5.0 left over from other tooling, which does not satisfy ^7.6.3. All engines.cjs/manifests.cjs code that does `require('semver')` was therefore exercised only against an incompatible major version by coincidence, not against what the manifest actually declares.
semverDependency.verification: Reproduced empirically before fixing: `npm ls semver` on the pre-fix tree printed `semver@5.5.0 deduped invalid: "^7.6.3" from the root project`.
semverDependency.fix: Ran `npm install --ignore-scripts` at the repository root (no `--package-lock-only`, so node_modules was actually updated; `--ignore-scripts` prevents the still-present `postinstall -> bootstrap -> lerna bootstrap` chain from firing, since Task 0.2 does not own cutover). Root `workspaces` field, lerna.json, and child locks were left untouched.
semverDependency.result: node_modules/semver is now 7.8.5 (satisfies ^7.6.3). `npm ls semver` no longer reports it invalid. `git diff --stat -- package.json package-lock.json` shows exactly one added devDependency line in package.json and 386 changed lines in package-lock.json; every changed lockfile line is a `node_modules/**/semver` entry (verified by filtering the diff for `node_modules/` keys and confirming none are unrelated to semver) -- the change is the expected consequence of several already-nested `semver@^7.3.x`/`^7.3.4` consumers now deduping against the new root-hoisted 7.8.5 instead of carrying their own copies. No package other than semver's own nested copies was added, removed, or changed.

reviewFindingsAddressed.claim: Fail when any expected workspace manifest is missing; validate expected package identities instead of silently filtering missing files.
reviewFindingsAddressed.agreement: Agreed and confirmed. `run()` built its per-workspace manifest set with `declaredWorkspaces.filter(w => fs.existsSync(...))`, so a workspace listed in root `workspaces` whose package.json does not exist on disk was silently dropped from every subsequent check (compile membership, forbidden protocols, internal ranges) instead of failing. Nothing checked that a present manifest's own `name` field matched the identity its directory implies, either.
reviewFindingsAddressed.fix: Added `checkWorkspaceManifestsPresent` (reports each missing manifest as a named failure instead of filtering it out) and `checkWorkspaceIdentities` (fails when a manifest's `name` disagrees with the `@bitpay-labs/<directory>` convention every one of the 18 real packages follows -- confirmed directly against all 18 real package.json files before relying on the convention). Both are wired into `run()`.

run() fails on a missing workspace manifest instead of silently filtering it out
checkWorkspaceIdentities fails when a manifest name disagrees with its directory-implied identity

reviewFindingsAddressed.claim: Compare root/workspace dependency declarations and installation metadata against manifests. Matching names and versions alone allows stale locks to pass.
reviewFindingsAddressed.agreement: Agreed. `checkWorkspaceRecordsAndLinks` only compared each workspace's `name`/`version` between the lock record and the manifest. A workspace that added, removed, or re-ranged a dependency in its package.json without the lock being regenerated would keep an identical name/version and pass, even though npm's own lock format mirrors each package's dependency tables into its lock record (confirmed by inspecting the real root lock's own `packages['']` entry, which mirrors root package.json's `dependencies`/`devDependencies` verbatim).
reviewFindingsAddressed.fix: Added `checkWorkspaceDependencyDeclarationsMatchManifest`, comparing `dependencies`/`devDependencies`/`peerDependencies`/`optionalDependencies` recorded in each workspace's lock record against its live manifest, field by field.
fixtures: checkWorkspaceDependencyDeclarationsMatchManifest passes when the lock mirrors the manifest exactly
checkWorkspaceDependencyDeclarationsMatchManifest fails when the manifest gained a dependency the lock never recorded
checkWorkspaceDependencyDeclarationsMatchManifest fails when a dependency range was edited without regenerating the lock
reviewFindingsAddressed.realRepoSpotCheck: lock.log: still exactly 36 real-repo failures (root lock has no workspace records at all pre-cutover, so the new check's early-continue-on-missing-record path is what's exercised; no double-counting or new noise).

reviewFindingsAddressed.claim: Read actual installed manifests, resolve workspace links, and fail on missing required packages. Currently, incompatible installed engines and absent dependencies can pass because checks use lock metadata.
reviewFindingsAddressed.agreement: Agreed on the core point, confirmed against the acceptance spec's own text (bitcore-acceptance-spec.md §3: 'Use the root lock as the installation inventory and actual installed manifests as the engine declarations... Missing required packages fail separately'). The implementation read `record.engines.node` from the lock's cached copy rather than the installed package's own package.json, and a non-optional dependency listed in the lock but absent from node_modules was evaluated against stale lock data instead of failing outright. Disagreed with reading 'resolve workspace links' as requiring this check to walk into workspace-link node_modules entries: those links point at workspace packages already governed by the root engines.node policy in `manifests`, and v3's flat lock format already lists every real nested dependency as its own top-level key, so no coverage gap was found there; that skip is left as-is.
reviewFindingsAddressed.fix: `collectInstalledEngineDeclarations` now reads `engines.node` from the installed package's real `package.json` on disk (falling back to the lock's copy only if that file can't be read at all), and separately collects/reports non-optional dependencies that are recorded in the lock but missing on disk.

reviewFindingsAddressed.claim: Validate declared main/types, recursively check copied templates, verify the CLI launcher is tracked and the root bin targets it, and execute --help with failure propagation.
reviewFindingsAddressed.agreement: Agreed on every sub-point, each reproduced directly against the real repository before fixing:

subFindings.realRepoReproduction: packages/bitcore-wallet-client/package.json declares `types: "ts_build/src/index.d.js"` (the exact typo the migration plan itself calls out as a pre-existing defect). The old checker never read `manifest.types` for TS_INDEX_REQUIREMENTS packages -- it only checked a hardcoded `ts_build/src/index.d.ts` path, which exists (the compiler emits .d.ts). Confirmed by `ls`: `.d.ts` exists, `.d.js` does not, and the pre-fix `verify.cjs artifacts --stage=build` produced zero failures for wallet-client.
subFindings.fix: Added `checkDeclaredEntryPoints`, run unconditionally for every workspace, which checks that `manifest.main` and `manifest.types` (whichever are declared) actually resolve on disk -- independent of the per-package hardcoded compiled-output tables.
subFindings.fixture: runBuildStage fails when a manifest declares a `types` path that does not exist, even though the compiled index does
subFindings.realRepoSpotCheck: artifacts-build.log now reports this exact real defect: `[artifacts] Declared package \`types\` does not resolve. workspace: packages/bitcore-wallet-client expected: "ts_build/src/index.d.js"`.

subFindings.realRepoReproduction: `checkTemplatesCopied` compared `fs.readdirSync(sourceDir)` top-level entry names only. A locale directory (e.g. `en/`) existing in both source and built output would pass even if a specific file inside it was never copied or diverged in content.
subFindings.fix: Replaced the shallow listing with `listFilesRecursively`, which walks the full tree and compares relative file paths, then hashes source vs. built content for every file (not just directory names) the same way the existing test-fixture stage already did.
subFindings.fixture: runBuildStage detects a template file nested in a locale subdirectory that was not copied

subFindings.point: Verify the CLI launcher is tracked and the root bin targets it
subFindings.realRepoReproduction: `bin/bitcore-cli` exists on disk in the real repo (left over from a prior build's `createBin`) but is untracked by git -- exactly the Task 1.5 defect the plan describes. The old check only asked `fs.existsSync`, which is true for an untracked file too, so it silently passed. Separately, the old check verified only that whatever `node_modules/.bin/bitcore-cli` pointed at was executable, never that it was the tracked launcher specifically.
subFindings.fix: Added `isGitTracked` (via `git ls-files --error-unmatch`, skipped only when `rootDir` isn't a git checkout at all, e.g. a synthetic fixture) and a realpath-equality check between the root `.bin` entry and the tracked launcher.

subFindings.fix: Added a `spawnSync(rootBin, ['--help'])` call (bounded by a 30s timeout) once the root `.bin` entry is confirmed to target the tracked launcher and be executable; a nonzero exit or spawn error is reported as a failure.

reviewFindingsAddressed.claim: Supplement lexical alias detection with actual consumer-originating Node resolution. Report lexical and canonical paths for every internal edge.
reviewFindingsAddressed.agreement: Agreed, and confirmed directly against the acceptance spec's own text (§4: 'Resolution originates from each consumer via createRequire or the appropriate ESM mechanism' and 'it records both [paths] for every internal edge' -- not only failing edges). Disagreed with treating the existing manual directory-search algorithm as itself a defect: it is a deliberate, documented substitute for `require.resolve`'s default symlink canonicalization, which would otherwise erase the lexical/canonical distinction this whole mode exists to catch; that part was kept as-is.
fix: Added `checkEntryPointResolution`, which -- once the directory-level check already confirms a dependency resolves to the correct real package -- additionally calls `require.resolve(targetName, { paths: [consumerDir] })` from the consumer's own directory to resolve the target's actual declared entry point (only when the target declares `main`/`exports`; a plain JS workspace with no declared entry point is left to the directory-level check, consistent with how `artifacts` treats such packages). This never imports/executes the target module.

Added a `report` array to `run()`'s return value recording `{workspace, consumer, lexicalPath, realPath, ok}` for every internal edge examined, success or failure, plus an opt-in `VERIFY_LINKS_REPORT=1` verbose-print path in verify.cjs's CLI dispatcher.
fixtures: run() also resolves the target's declared entry point via consumer-originating Node resolution
run() fails when a target declares an entry point that does not actually resolve
run() records both the lexical and canonical path for every internal edge, not only failing ones
reviewFindingsAddressed.realRepoSpotCheck: links.log: still 29 real-repo failures, identical in count and content to the prior revision (all pre-existing multi-alias findings under the current per-package Lerna bootstrap layout). The new entry-point-resolution check ran across every real internal edge without throwing or adding noise, since Lerna's bootstrap-created aliases do point at genuinely built packages in the current tree.
